observations: A horned head and upper-body form occupy the center and right of a near-total black field, built from overlapping short strokes in dark olive, teal, and orange that leave no single clean edge; shoulders and arm-like forms are partially visible but the lower body is cut by the image edge.
Two large circular glows sit where eyes would be, radiating amber-yellow light outward and casting a faint halo across the upper chest and muzzle area.
Bold orange-red lettering reading 'STILL BULLISH @NIFTYINK' occupies the lower-left quadrant, drawn in a thick outlined style that contrasts with the loose mark-making of the figure.
reading: The figure emerges from black almost entirely through its own light — two burning eye-circles pull surrounding strokes into visibility. Dark olive and teal marks describe bulk without resolving into smooth form, and a partially visible jaw adds a raw edge. The text in the lower left reads as declaration rather than caption, its solid outlines sitting apart from the figure's restless surface.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between #99 and #101 in both title and recorded creation order. Neighbor #99 uses a pale ground with diffuse light; #101 strips to flat black-and-yellow — making #100 the darkest and most internally lit of the three.

connections.reason: Both works place a heavily stroked figure against a dark surround with warm amber-gold marks concentrated at the center, though #138 adds a red-orange background wash absent from #100's pure black field.

In #99 the eyes are large orange-red ovals on a light ground; in #100 the same feature becomes self-luminous amber circles against black — a direct contrast in how glowing eyes anchor each composition.

lookingQuestion: Where exactly does the light from the eyes stop — and what marks, if any, remain visible beyond that boundary?
ambiguities: The lower body is cut by the image edge; only shoulders and arm-like forms are partially visible, so the full extent and posture of the figure cannot be confirmed.
The species or character type is not fully resolved; pointed ears, horns, and jaw shape suggest a non-human creature but mark density obscures confirmation.
The lettering 'STILL BULLISH @NIFTYINK' is treated as embedded content per curatorial guidelines, not as an artist statement or title.
